entries.title: Rear main seal leak; upper seal half siliconed in
entries.text: The rear main seal leaked. A previous owner had siliconed the upper seal half into the block. The lower half came out of the cap but the upper half would not move, so the crank has to come out. (Date approximate: start of the chat.)

entries.title: Chip broke off the rear of the block
entries.text: While punching out the old seal, a chip broke off the very rear of the block, transmission side. Believed non-structural; whether it reaches the seal groove has not been checked. (Date approximate; from the earlier chat.)

entries.title: Crank turned a couple of times with the chain off
entries.text: The crank was turned a couple of times after the chain was off. It turned smoothly with no hard stop, so valve contact is very unlikely. Confirm with a compression or leak-down test after reassembly. Don't turn the crank again until it's out; when it goes back in, set the keyway to match the dot-to-dot photo before the chain goes on.

entries.title: A couple of small nicks on the crank journals
entries.text: Journal cleanup started: knock down raised burrs with oiled 400-600 grit, finish with crocus cloth. Measurements wait on the micrometer. (Date approximate; the Nov 2 work suggests the crank is out.)

entries.title: Status: torn down on the stand, waiting on parts
entries.text: Summit cart held the micrometer (SUM-900014, $64.99), assembly lube and four gaskets (fuel pump, oil pump, water pump, timing cover); ZDDP additive recommended. The rear main seal and oil pan gasket were not in the cart. Next: micrometer arrives, measure journals, order bearings, water pump and timing cover.

entries.title: Old high-school accessory wiring removed
entries.text: The add-on accessory wiring from high school has been removed. Exact date not recorded.

entries.title: Test setup with the engine out
entries.text: With the engine out the body has no factory ground (normally battery negative -> engine -> ground cable at the starter-relay mounting bolt -> body). A temporary jumper now runs from battery negative to that cable at the relay bolt; grounding battery negative to another body point did not work (poor contact). The ground cable's engine end is loose. The starter cable is kept off the relay or insulated. Ignition switch and headlight switch are out of the dash; both front parking/turn connectors are unplugged at the wheel wells. Dates approximate (testing ran Nov 11-12).

entries.title: Starter relay terminal behavior verified
entries.text: Fender-mounted relay, left to right: battery stud, S, I, starter stud; it grounds through its mounting bolt. Battery stud (black/yellow, circuit 37) is hot always. S (red/blue) is hot only in START. I (brown, joined to the pink resistance wire at the firewall main disconnect) is 12 V in ON (through the coil feed) and in START. Starter stud is hot only while cranking.

entries.title: Loose solid-red wire at the relay reads 0 V everywhere
entries.text: A solid-red wire comes from the same firewall main disconnect as the S, I and battery-stud wires. Its relay end is loose and it reads 0 V in every key position. Not identified; trace it with the wiring diagram before connecting it anywhere.

measurements.location: Starter relay end, every key position

entries.title: Ignition switch positions and accessory eyelet
entries.text: Bezel positions are ACC - OFF - ON - START (spring-loaded). An unmarked cylinder-release position counter-clockwise past ACC was mistaken for ACC and caused confusing readings; ignore it. The plug fits one way; a separate eyelet terminal on the back is the accessory feed, circuit 297 (black-green), which feeds the turn-signal flasher (circuit 8). Verified with correct positions: S hot only in START; pink coil feed and brown hot in ON and START.

entries.title: Pink resistance wire: 12 V unloaded, lower under coil load
entries.text: The pink resistance wire reads a full 12 V unloaded. Under coil load it drops to roughly 6-9 V. Never use it as a switched-power source for accessories.

measurements.what: Pink resistance wire, under coil load
measurements.location: Coil feed; roughly 6-9 V (approximate, no single reading recorded)

entries.title: Headlight switch crackles and breaker cycles in the parking position
entries.text: In the parking (middle) position the headlight switch crackled and its breaker made a ding; the taillights blinked as the breaker reset, and the front parking lights never lit.

entries.title: Short on circuit 11 isolated to the passenger front parking wiring
entries.text: The short to ground is on circuit 11 (front parking lights), in the passenger-side wiring past the wheel-well connector. Unplugging that connector stopped the crackling; unplugging the driver side did not. Next: battery off, bulb out, ohm wire 11 to ground to find the spot.

entries.title: Crackle at the starter relay was arcing at the ground bolt
entries.text: The crackle heard at the starter relay was arcing at the relay-bolt ground connection, with short-circuit current returning through it. It was not the relay switching. Clean and tighten that ground.

entries.title: Headlight switch continuity map: switch looks fine
entries.text: From the owner's chart (see photo). Battery (B) connects to A in Off (plus I-R through the dash-light dimmer); to R, P, I, A in the middle (park) position; to R, H, I, A fully out (headlights). P is front parking (live only in the middle position; they go off when the headlights come on), R is taillights, H headlights, I instrument lights, D1/D2 likely dome/courtesy, A unconfirmed. The switch appears to work as designed.

entries.title: Dash-light feed is a blue wire, not a ground
entries.text: The blue dash-light wire with a three-way splitter reads grounded with the lights off (through the dash bulbs) and is powered, dimmed by the headlight knob, with the lights on. It is not a ground. It has a spare unused branch, a good source for the tach light and radio illumination.

entries.title: Brake lights work: rear wiring, sockets and bulbs are good
entries.text: Proves the rear wiring, sockets and bulbs, and the turn-signal switch's brake contacts.

entries.title: Flasher confirmed good, and its feed (circuit 8)
entries.text: A jumper test made a rear light blink through the flasher. Orange-yellow (8) jumpered to a rear pin gave a steady light, so the flasher feed is confirmed.

entries.title: Blue (44) good to the four-wire connector; fronts read 0 V
entries.text: A jumper from the car side of the four-wire connector to a rear pin blinked, so blue (44) is good to that point. With the harness connected, blue reads 12 V at the connector, but white-blue (2) and green-white (3) read 0 V in every lever position. Conclusion: the fault is in the turn-signal switch or the blue pin's contact between the connector halves.

entries.title: Flasher terminals read 12 V with the key OFF (unexplained)
entries.text: Both flasher terminals read 12 V even with the key off. Per the diagram it is fed from the accessory circuit and should be dead in OFF. Not yet explained.

entries.title: Heater fan: motor, power and resistor work; factory switch never grounds
entries.text: The '66 blower is switched on the ground side (forum source): the motor has power on one wire and the switch grounds it through the resistor taps (high = no resistor). Grounding a resistor terminal with a jumper runs the fan, so motor, power and resistor are good. The factory switch, with its housing grounded, never grounds any output in any position. Decision: replace the heater fan switch.

entries.title: Uncle's potentiometer wiring removed from the heater fan
entries.text: The motor's control wire is now on the resistor.

entries.title: Testing lessons
entries.text: Continuity tests mislead wherever bulbs or motors are connected (cold filaments read near 0 ohm), so pull bulbs or unplug loads first. Use a current-limited test light, not a bare jumper, when hunting shorts. Battery disconnected: multimeter ohms/continuity. Battery connected: voltage or test light. Back-probing means sliding a thin probe in from behind beside the wire at a plugged-in connector.

entries.title: Ordered the micrometer set, assembly lube, and all gaskets and seals
entries.text: Includes the rear main seal, oil pan gasket set, front crank seal, and the fuel pump, oil pump, pickup, water pump, timing cover, thermostat and valve cover gaskets. Still to order: water pump, new timing cover, and bearings once the journals are measured.
